subject: Cognitive Science
title: Prototype Theory
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Prototype Theory.

hook.text: Ask people to name a bird and most say robin, not penguin. Some members just feel more "birdy."

buildup.text: Eleanor Rosch proposed that categories cluster around a best example—a prototype.

discovery.text: You judge new items by similarity to the prototype. Robin-like things feel more like birds.

twist.text: This explains why people rate chairs as better furniture than rugs, even though both qualify.

climax.text: Categories are graded, not binary. Membership comes in degrees of typicality.

punchline.text: Some members are more "in" than others.
